chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūs al-Khalanjī, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Layth al-Murādī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who mounted an orphan boy on a horse that he had hired for a wage, and that was the livelihood of that boy, while his agnate relatives knew of that. Then he made him run in the racecourse, and the horse struck a man and killed him. Upon whom is his blood-money? He said: “Upon the owner of the horse.” I said: “What if the horse threw the boy and killed him?” He said: “There is nothing upon the owner of the horse.”

key_terms.الْحَلْبَةِ: the racecourse or place of racing
key_terms.بِأُجْرَةٍ: for a wage, showing that the matter involves hired labor and livelihood
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: his blood-money, the financial compensation due for a killing
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْفَرَسِ: the owner of the horse, identified here as the liable party in one case
key_terms.عَصَبَتُهُ: his agnate relatives or paternal kin
key_terms.يَتِيمًا: an orphan boy, indicating the child’s vulnerable legal and social status

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for blood-money if a hired horse kills someone or throws and kills its rider according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses liability in a case involving a hired horse, an orphan boy, and accidental killing. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that the blood-money for a man killed by the horse is upon the horse’s owner, while if the horse throws and kills the boy, nothing is due from the owner in that case.
